FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Printing Inks, Stationery and Allied Product Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical 
Division Council. 


This standard was originally published in 1963 and is being revised to update the standard incorporating two 
amendments issued till date. This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions relating to the 
material. 


An Indian standard on school chalks will ensure satisfactory quality of school chalks and would be valuable to 
those concerned with the purchasing of equipment for schools. This standard while prescribes such requirements 
as would ensure satisfactory quality of school chalks, it is necessary to mention that different results may be 
obtained on different blackboard surfaces. It is, therefore, suggested that chalks complying with the requirements 
of this standard may be tried on the surfaces on which they are to be used before making a final choice. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 “Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)”. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 2694 : 2018 


Indian Standard 


SCHOOL CHALKS, MOULDED, WHITE — 
SPECIFICATION 
( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements, methods of 
sampling and tests for moulded white chalks intended 
primarily for writing on blackboards in school. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given below contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of these standards: 


Title 
grade 


IS No. 


IS 1070 : 1992 Reagent water (third 


revision) 


IS 460 (Part 1): Test sieves: Part 1 Wire cloth test 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Materials 


Chalks shall be made from good quality calcined 
gypsum reasonably free from poisonous and toxic 
materials, injurious to human beings. They shall be of 
homogeneous mass free from grease, grit and sandy 
abrasives. 


3.2 Finish 


Chalks shall be circular in cross section and tapered at 
one end, and shall be smooth uniform shape and size. 
They shall be free from external blow holes. 


3.3 Hardness 


Chalks shall also produce freely, without scratching or 
otherwise harming the blackboards, visible and distinct 
marks that can be easily erased with a piece of dry cloth. 


3.4 Chalks shall also conform to the requirements 


1985 sieves (third revision) given in Table 1 when tested according to the methods 
prescribed in Annex A. Reference to the relevant 
clauses of Annex A is given in column 4 of the table. 

Table 1 Requirements for School Chalks, Moulded, White

4 SAMPLING 


Representative samples of the material shall be drawn 
and adjudged as prescribed in Annex B. 


5 MARKING 


5.1 Each container shall have the following information 
marked on a name plate in a permanent and legible 
manner in a location where it is accessible and visible: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Indication of the source of manufacture and trade- 
mark, if any; 

c) Number of chalks in the container; 


d) Batch number or lot number in code or otherwise; 
and 


e) Month and year of manufacture. 
5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The containers may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 
and the Rules and Regulations made there under. The 
details ofthe conditions under which the licence for use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 


6 PACKING AND PACKAGING 


Chalks shall be packed in suitable paperboard 
containers which offer adequate protection to the chalks 
during transportation. Chalks shall be tightly packed 
in the container and saw dust or other cushioning 
materials shall be used to fill up the empty spaces to 
prevent breakage. Unless otherwise, agreed to between 
the purchaser and supplier, each box shall contain 
100 chalks. 


IS 2694 : 2018 


ANNEX A 
(Clause 3.4) 


TESTS FOR SCHOOL CHALKS, MOULDED, WHITE 


A-1 DETERMINATION 
SULPHATE CONTENT 


OF CALCIUM 


A-1.1 Reagents 


A-1.1.1 Quality of Reagents — Pure chemicals and 
distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be used in the test. 


NOTE — “Pure Chemicals” shall mean chemicals that do not 

contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 
A-1.1.2 Ammonium Acetate Solution — Dissolve 454 g 
of ammonium acetate in two litres of water. Add 
ammonium hydroxide to make the solution distinctly 
ammoniacal. 


A-1.1.3 Diatomaceous Silica — Wash kieselguhr free 
from soluble matter and dry to constant mass at 105°C 
to 110°C. 


A-1.1.4 Ammonium Hydroxide — 20 percent (v/v). 


A-1.1.5 Ammonium Wash Solution — Dilute 100 ml of 
ammonium hydroxide to one litre of distilled water. 


A-1.2 Procedure 


Grind the sample in a mortar pestle so as to pass 
through 250 micron IS Sieve (see Note). Place about 
4 g of the sieved sample, accurately weighed, in 
a 600 ml beaker. Add 350 ml of ammonium acetate 
solution and stir the mixture thoroughly so as to loosen 
the matter from the bottom of the beaker. Add about 
0.2 g of diatomaceous silica, accurately weighed, 
to the mixture and heat at 70°C on a steam-bath for 
30 minutes with frequent stirring. Keep the solution 
distinctly ammoniacal during this period by adding 
ammonium hydroxide, if necessary. Filter the mixture 
through a weighed Gooch crucible applying suction, 
if necessary. During filtration, stir frequently to keep 
the diatomaceous earth suspended in the liquid. Wash 
the residue five times, each with 10 ml of ammonium 
acetate solution, after thoroughly draining of each 
washing. Repeat washing with eight 10 ml portions of 
ammonia wash solution. Dry the crucible in an oven at 
70°C to constant mass. 

NOTE — For size grading IS sieves conforming to 

IS 460 (Part 1) : 1985 “Test Sieves: Part-I Wire Cloth Test 

Sieves” are specified. Where these sieves are not available, 


other equivalent standard sieves as judged by the aperture may 
be used. 


A-1.3 Calculation 
Calcium sulphate, percent by mass = 
100 x {4-(B-C)}-M 
A 


where, 
A = mass of the material taken for the test, in g; 
B = final mass of the crucible and the contents 
after drying, in g; 
C = initial mass of the crucible plus mass of 
diatomaceous silica used as filter aid, in g; and 
M = percentage of free moisture (see A-2.2). 


A-2 DETERMINATION OF FREE MOISTURE 


A-2.1 Procedure 


Grind four chalks in a mortar pestle so as to pass 
through 1.00 mm IS Sieve [see IS 460 (Part 1)]. Weigh 
accurately about 10 g of the ground sample and spread 
itin a layer in a petri dish. Place it in an oven maintained 
at 100° + 2°C till constant mass is obtained. 


A-2.2 Calculation 


Moisture, percent by mass = 


100 (A-B) 
A 


where, 
A = mass of the ground material taken for the test, 
in g; and 


B=mass of the material after drying, in g. 


A-3 MEASUREMENT OF LENGTH AND 
DIAMETER 


A-3.1 Procedure 

Measure the length and diameter at two ends of only 
full length chalk by means of calipers and a foot-rule 
calibrated in millimetres or with a sliding caliper 
gauge. 


A-4 DETERMINATION OF MASS 
A-4.1 Procedure 


Weigh 10 chalks, drawn randomly from the same 
box (see B-2.2) at a time and compute the mass per 
100 chalks for each box. 


A-4.1.1 The mass computed for each box selected 
for tests (see B-2.2) shall not be differ by more than 
2 percent from the average. 


IS 2694 : 2018 


A-5 DETERMINATION OF TRANSVERSE 
BREAKING STRENGTH 


A-5.1 Apparatus 


The apparatus as shown in Fig. 1 shall be of such 
construction that a stick of chalk can be supported at 
two points, 63 mm apart and weight applied by means 
of a loading anvil midway between the two supports 
and at right angles to the chalk. The assembly consisting 
of the loading anvil, spindle, and weight platform, 
shall weigh approximately 500 g. The weight shall be 
applied either by the use of lead shot (pre-weighed) or 
by the use of standard weights. 


A-5.2 Procedure 


Before testing, dry the chalks at 38° + 3°C for a period 
of 24 hours to ensure that they are completely dry. Place 
the chalk in position on the two supporting points so that 
the central axis of the chalks is horizontal. Then lower 
the loading anvil carefully until it rests on the chalk 
in the middle. Add one by one suitable mass carefully 
to the weight platform until the chalk breaks. The 
transverse breaking strength of the chalk shall be sum 
of mass of the loading anvil, spindle, weight platform, 
and any additional mass on the weight platform. 


WEIGHT PLATFORM 


Fic 1. APPRATUS FOR DETERMINATION OF TRANSVERSE BREAKING STRENGTH

ANNEXB 
(Clause 6.1) 


SAMPLING OF SCHOOL CHALKS, MOULDED, WHITE 


B-1 GENRAL PRECAUTIONS 


B-1.1 Samples shall be drawn from originally unopened 
and undamaged boxes. 


B-1.2 Samples shall be protected from abnormal 
exposure to heat, and shall not be allowed to come in 
contact with any liquid. 


B-1.3 Samples shall be handled as little as possible, and 
contact with wet or sweated hands shall be avoided. 


B-2 SCALE OF SAMPLING 


B-2.1 Lot 


In any consignment, all boxes of school chalks drawn 
from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. 
If the consignment is declared or known to consist of 
different batches of manufacture, the boxes belonging 
to the same batch shall be grouped together and each 
such group shall constitute a separate lot. 


B-2.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the 
requirements of the specification, tests shall be carried 
out of each lot separately. The number of boxes to be 
selected from lots of different sizes shall be in accordance 
with Table 2. From each selected box, 10 chalks 
shall be picked up at random. 


Table 2 Scale of Sampling and Permissible 
Number of Defectives 


(Clause B-2.2) 


No. of Boxes No. of Total No. of Permissible 
in the Lot Boxes to be Chalks to be No. of 
(N) Selected Selected Defective 
(n) Chalks 
(1) (2) (3) (4) 
Up to 5 1 10 0 
6,, 50 3 30 1 
51 „100 5 50 2 
101 ,, 500 10 100 4 
More than 500 15 150 6 


B-2.2.1 The boxes shall be selected at random and 
to ensure randomness of selection, the following 
procedure is recommended for use: 


Count the boxes in a systematic manner as 1, 2, 3,... 
up to r and so no, where, r is the integral part of N n 
( N and n being the number of boxes in the lot and 
number of boxes to be selected respectively ). Every 
rth box thus counted shall be selected till the requisite 
number of boxes is obtained. 


From each of the boxes thus selected, 10 chalks shall be 
picked up blind from different places. 


B-3 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY 


B-3.1 All the chalks selected according to B-2.2 shall be 
examined for finish (see 3.2). Ifthe number of defectives 
found is equal to or less than the corresponding number 
given in column 4 of Table 2, the lot shall be declared 
as conforming to the specification requirements in 3.2 
and 3.3. 


B-3.2 All the chalks selected according to B-2.2 shall 
than be examined for length of the stick and diameter at 
the two ends. Any chalk failing to meet the requirement 
of either length or diameter shall be considered as a 
defective. 


B-3.2.1 If the number of defective chalks found is less 
than or equal to the corresponding number given in 
column 4 of Table 2, the lot shall be deemed to have 
satisfied the dimensional requirement for the chalks. 


B-3.3 The chalks in the sample shall be massed in group 
of 10 and each group shall satisfy the requirement in 
Table 1, item (v) (see also A-4.1). 


B-3.4 Calcium sulphate content and free moisture 
content shall be determined on a suitable number of 
chalks after crushing them to the required fineness, 
as indicated in A-1 and A-2 respectively. Five chalks 
shall be selected from those got according to B-2.2 
and subjected to transverse breaking strength test 
separately. 


B-3.4.1 A lot shall be declared as conforming to the 
requirements of calcium sulphate, moisture content 
and transverse breaking strength if all the test results, 
obtained, as under B-3.4 are found satisfactory. 


B-3.5 A lot shall be declared to have met the requirement 
of the specification if, the stipulations laid down in 
B-3.1 to B-3.4.1 are all fulfilled.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards

“BIS Catalogue” and “Standards: Monthly Additions’.
